notes: `לּוֹ` and its suffix are both `unrepresented`: the ASV's *in such a case* renders `כָּכָה`, with the supplied preposition and generic noun joining that unit under rules 33 and 31 and the copula under rule 20, and nothing is written for the dative (rule 40's closing sentence).
The supplied *Yea* opening the second colon is `added`; no conjunction morpheme stands there (rule 14).
`שֶׁ` fuses with the resumptive 3ms suffix on `אֱלֹהָיו` as one *whose* under rule 22, headed on the relative.

The copula of the last clause is placed on `אֱלֹהָיו`, read as the Hebrew predicate on the model of rule 20's `יְהוָה הוּא נַחֲלָתוֹ` → *Jehovah is their inheritance*; the competing reading, following the English word order onto the divine name, is named in the unit's note.
